Tomato petiole cut-point VLM: pipeline and results

2026-09-17 · progress report · sim-vlm branch, commit ec0a5b0

RGB(-D) robot-head image + query pixel → cut point in pixels (and depth) or abstain.

  • Synthetic Isaac Sim greenhouse, RB-Y1 head D405 camera, 848×408, native metric depth.
  • Release visible_occluded_20260911_v1: 14,259 rows, 24 plants, geometry-derived labels.
  • Six fine-tunes of Qwen3-VL-8B (RGB) and of the 3D HAMSTER planner (RGB + depth); same recipe, same held-out plants.
  • Best model: 3D HAMSTER init. Occlusion-decision AUC 0.63 → 0.88, median cut error 18 → 13.6 px.

1 · Task

  • Input: one unaltered 848×408 RGB frame (+ native depth for RGB-D models) and a query pixel on the target petiole, ≥45 mm from the attachment and ≥18 px from the cut.
  • Output: JSON: status (localized | abstain), cut point (or null), visibility, next action. Coordinates normalized to [0,1000).
  • Label convention: nominal cut = 10 mm along the petiole from the main-stem junction; admissible interval 10–20 mm (yellow). Hidden cut region → abstain.
  • Scale: the 10 mm interval projects to ~8.5 px (0.85 px/mm); petioles are 4–5 px wide.

System prompt (Qwen runs):

You localize a synthetic tomato petiole cut point in a robot-head RGB image. The user supplies a normalized query coordinate on the target petiole, NOT the cut point. Trace that petiole to its junction with the main stem. A localized target must be traceable through visible petiole pixels from the query to the cut region. The dataset convention places the nominal cut 10 mm along the petiole toward the leaves from its attachment; 10-20 mm is the evaluation interval, not a spherical tolerance. Use visual evidence. If the cut region is occluded or cannot be distinguished, abstain instead of inventing coordinates. Coordinates (query and cut_point_uv) are normalized continuous coordinates in [0,1000), top-left edge origin, x right and y down: x_norm=1000*x/848 and y_norm=1000*y/408 for the ORIGINAL 848x408 image, independent of processor resizing. Return ONLY JSON with exactly these keys: status (localized or abstain), cut_point_uv (a two-number normalized coordinate array or null), visibility (clear, partial, or occluded), next_action (inspect_cut_region or change_viewpoint). This is perception only; never claim that a blade motion is safe or executable.

2 · How the data was collected

  1. Assets: 24 component-level tomato plants (manifest with attachment points, axes, capsule centrelines; 870 intact leaf-bearing candidates audited, 971 stubs excluded).
  2. Scene: the greenhouse package with the RB-Y1 seated on the floor by triangle hits; floor-aligned base/torso stances; head D405 render product at 848×408 (pinhole f=470.9 px).
  3. Views: a deterministic scheduler samples bounded robot stances and head poses per target (up to 160 candidate views for training families, 64 for held-out), four serial lanes with exit receipts and independent audits.
  4. Per frame: lossless RGB, Replicator distance_to_image_plane float32 depth + validity, instance masks, intrinsics/extrinsics, robot joint state, asset hashes.
  5. Labels: geometry projects the 10 mm point and the 10–20 mm interval; native masks + camera-Z decide visible vs occluded; a query point is chosen on the visible distal petiole and screened for size, contrast and exposure. Ambiguous cases are excluded, never labelled.
  6. QA: hash-bound review cards; 136 assistant-reviewed accepts, 21 holds/rejects enforced at source level. No per-image human review.

5 · Training

Objective: supervised fine-tuning; cross-entropy on the assistant answer tokens only (prompt and image masked), mean per example; 32 examples per optimizer step on 4× H200 (DeepSpeed ZeRO-2 for full fine-tunes); BF16, cosine schedule, 3% warmup, clip 1.0, seed 41.

  • Gates before every multi-GPU run: real-processor loss-mask check, 2-step smoke, 32-example overfit, fresh-process reload with greedy generation.
  • v2 changes: rounding coordinates (57 → 36 answer tokens) so digit noise stops dominating the loss; class balance; up-weighted status tokens.
  • hamster-01 predicts the cut point and its depth (native depth at the label pixel); occluded → point_3d: null. Same LR, epochs, weights as v2.

6 · Evaluation protocol

  • Set: validation split, 1,358 rows, 39 targets on 4 plants never seen in training. Test split never read.
  • Decoding: greedy, batch 1, same prompt as training. Answers parsed and converted back to pixels; invalid JSON, out-of-frame points or inconsistent status/action count as failures (never repaired).
  • Decision metrics: abstain accuracy on the 346 occluded rows; coverage on the 1,012 visible rows; balanced accuracy = their mean (chance 0.5); probe AUC = ranking quality of the model's own log P(abstain) − log P(localized), independent of the decoding threshold.
  • Localization metrics: median pixel error of answers; within 5 px; within 2 px of the projected 10–20 mm interval (the cut criterion).
  • Baselines: untuned model; image-free shortcuts (constant point, copy query, query + median offset, always abstain).
  • Per-target macro averages are reported alongside per-row numbers, since a target has ~40 views.

Same rows, split, recipe and scorer; only the backbone and depth input differ. Per-target macro balanced accuracy 0.628 → 0.749. Predictions are not query copies (median 60 px from the query, same as the labels).

  • Occlusion is finally a visual cue. RGB fine-tunes stall at AUC 0.58–0.64 on unseen plants (0.78 on training rows). hamster-01 reaches 0.884.
  • Greedy under-abstains (16% vs 25% base rate). Thresholding the point/null log-odds at the base rate: abstain 0.685, false localization 0.315, coverage 0.892, balanced 0.789.
  • Precision improved, not solved: within 5 px 0.047 → 0.125; inside the interval 0.027 → 0.052.
  • Depth output is coarse (median 2.4 cm error); the native-depth gate still helps (false loc. 0.46 → 0.34).
  • Feeding depth as an image to the RGB tower (v3) did not help; a trained depth pathway did.

9 · Example outputs (hamster-01, validation)

Cyan = prediction. Order: correct localization; miss on the wrong structure; correct abstention; fabricated point on an occluded target.

10 · Failure points and what they imply

  1. Answers miss the petiole. Only 10% of v2 answers on visible targets land on the target mask; misses sit ~1.4 m behind on the background. hamster-01 halves the error but 95% of answers are still outside the 10–20 mm interval.
  2. Abstention is calibrated, not solved. Best balanced accuracy 0.79 with a tuned threshold; 31% of occluded targets still get a point.
  3. Dataset ceiling. 168 training targets behind 11,520 rows; 10/39 validation targets are abstain-only; per-plant abstain rate 0.01–0.43 (identity predicts the label); cue is ~8 px beside a fruit/stem edge; no medium class.

Re-collection priorities

  1. Targets over views: cap ~10–15 views per target; grow targets (870 audited candidates) and plants.
  2. View-dependent occlusion per target; no target abstain-only; balance per plant.
  3. Add medium/partial and the other negatives (invalid candidate, no target, out of view).
  4. Keep metric depth aligned to RGB and depth at the label point: the chosen backbone consumes and predicts it.
  5. Query-centred crop as a second input; per-target evaluation; human-verified held-out occlusion labels.

Deployable rule for the current model: propose (hamster-01) → threshold the abstain log-odds → native-depth consistency gate → execution layer. Not yet qualified to command a cut.
